must_have: Identifiable at-fault party or liable entity
Documented physical injury or verifiable medical treatment
Incident date within applicable SOL for the jurisdiction
Clear causal link between incident and claimed injuries
nice_to_have: Insurance policy details for all parties
auto_decline: SOL expired with no viable tolling theory
No compensable injury (property-only with no injury claim)
Client solely at fault with no comparative-fault recovery path
Conflict of interest with existing client or adverse party
Estimated recoverable damages below firm minimum ($7,500)
intake_questions: When and where did the incident occur?
Who do you believe was at fault and why?
What injuries did you sustain and what treatment have you received?
Have you spoken to any insurance adjusters or signed any releases?

must_have: Employer–employee or covered-worker relationship
Specific adverse action, discrimination, harassment, or wage claim theory
Incident(s) within administrative and civil filing deadlines
Named employer and work location/jurisdiction
nice_to_have: Offer letters, handbooks, and employment contracts
Emails, texts, or HR complaints documenting the issue
EEOC/DFEH/CRD charge filing confirmation if already filed
auto_decline: Claim is exclusively workers’ compensation with no dual-capacity exception
Administrative deadline missed and no equitable tolling argument
Client still employed and seeks only informal advice with no claim intent
Conflict of interest with employer client of the firm
Independent contractor with no viable misclassification or statutory claim
intake_questions: What is your job title and employment status (current/former)?
What adverse action or violation occurred, and on what dates?
Did you report the issue internally or to a government agency?
Are you seeking reinstatement, wages, damages, or something else?

must_have: Clear immigration goal (visa, adjustment, asylum, removal defense, naturalization)
Client identity and current immigration status (or lack thereof)
Country of nationality and any prior USCIS/EOIR history known to client
No conflict with existing immigration clients in related proceedings
nice_to_have: Family relationship evidence for petition-based cases
auto_decline: Matter requires only notario/document-prep services outside attorney practice
Client seeks advice on committing immigration fraud
Firm lacks capacity for imminent removal hearing (under 14 days) without coverage
Conflict of interest with petitioner/sponsor already represented by firm adverse to client
intake_questions: What immigration benefit or defense do you need?
What is your current status and when did you last enter the U.S.?
Have you ever been detained, removed, or received a Notice to Appear?
Do you have a sponsor, employer, or family petitioner involved?

must_have: Matter type identified (divorce, custody, support, DVRO, adoption, paternity)
Residency/jurisdiction basis in an active firm state
Names and relationships of all parties and minor children
No unwaived conflict with opposing party
nice_to_have: Existing court orders or prior case numbers
Parenting-time calendar and school/medical info for children
auto_decline: Out-of-state custody matter with no UCCJEA home-state basis for our jurisdiction
Client seeks assistance violating a protective order
Conflict of interest with spouse/partner already retained
Matter is purely amicable DIY paperwork with no counsel role requested
intake_questions: What family-law issue do you need help with?
Where do you and the other party currently live?
Are there minor children, and where have they lived for the past 6 months?
Are there existing orders, restraining orders, or open cases?

must_have: Pending charge, investigation, warrant, or post-conviction matter identified
Arrest/incident date and charging agency if known
Client is the accused (or authorized representative for a minor)
Court/jurisdiction where case is or will be heard
nice_to_have: Police report number and discovery already received
auto_decline: Client seeks advice on committing a future crime
Matter is outside active criminal jurisdictions and no pro hac vice plan
Conflict with co-defendant or victim already represented
Federal capital case outside firm capability
intake_questions: What are you charged with, or what are police investigating?
When is your next court date, and which courthouse?
Are you in custody, and what is your bail status?
Have you already spoken to police or prosecutors without counsel?

must_have: Work-related injury or occupational illness
Employer identity and approximate date of injury / last injurious exposure
Claim within jurisdictional filing windows or ongoing benefits dispute
Employee (or dependent) claimant status
nice_to_have: DWCs / state claim forms already filed
Medical reports and work status notes
auto_decline: Injury clearly not work-related and no occupational exposure theory
Claim filing deadline expired with no exception
Client is employer seeking defense counsel (plaintiff-side WC firm only)
Conflict with employer or carrier already represented
intake_questions: When and how were you hurt at work?
Did you report the injury to your employer, and when?
Are you receiving medical care or disability benefits now?
Has the claim been denied, delayed, or underpaid?

must_have: Identifiable healthcare provider or facility
Alleged deviation from standard of care with resulting injury
Treatment dates within SOL / repose rules for the jurisdiction
Signed medical authorization willingness for records review
nice_to_have: Names of treating and subsequent providers
Itemized medical bills and disability documentation
auto_decline: Bad outcome alone with no arguable negligence (known complication without breach)
SOL or statute of repose expired
Damages limited to dissatisfaction without compensable harm
Conflict with hospital/system that is a firm client
Estimated case value below firm med-mal minimum ($50,000) after cost analysis
intake_questions: Which provider or facility do you believe committed malpractice?
What treatment occurred, and what went wrong?
What injuries or additional treatment resulted?
When did you first suspect something was done incorrectly?

must_have: Identifiable product (brand/model if possible)
Injury or property damage caused by product defect, failure to warn, or breach of warranty
Product preserved or documented when feasible
Claim within SOL for the jurisdiction
nice_to_have: Product photos, serial numbers, packaging, manuals
Incident/medical reports linking product use to injury
auto_decline: Product discarded with no photos/identifiers and no other proof of defect
Injury from intentional misuse with no defective condition theory
SOL expired
Conflict with manufacturer already represented by firm
Estimated recoverable damages below firm minimum ($10,000)
intake_questions: What product caused the injury, and how was it being used?
Do you still have the product, packaging, or purchase proof?
What injuries resulted and what treatment did you receive?
Was there a recall or prior complaint about this product?

must_have: State actor or covered entity under federal/state civil-rights statutes
Specific rights violation theory (e.g., excessive force, unlawful search, discrimination, First Amendment retaliation)
Incident within SOL (often 2 years for §1983; state analogs vary)
Identifiable defendants or agency
nice_to_have: Bodycam / dashcam references or public records requests filed
auto_decline: Purely private dispute with no state action and no statutory coverage
SOL expired
Client seeks only criminal prosecution of officers (no civil claim)
Conflict with municipality/agency already represented
intake_questions: Which agency or officials were involved, and what did they do?
When and where did the incident occur?
Were you arrested, injured, or had property seized?
Have you filed an administrative claim against the public entity (if required)?

must_have: Consumer transaction or deceptive business practice involving the client
Specific statutory or common-law theory (UDAP/UCL, FCRA, FDCPA, lemon law, fraud)
Conduct within SOL
Identifiable business defendant
nice_to_have: Recordings or written communications with the business
auto_decline: Business-vs-business commercial dispute outside consumer statutes
Damages below small-claims / firm referral threshold with no class or fee-shift path
SOL expired
Conflict with defendant business that is a firm client
intake_questions: What product, service, or debt collection practice caused the problem?
What false statements, hidden fees, or unlawful collection acts occurred?
How much money did you lose or what credit harm did you suffer?
Have you already disputed the issue with the company or a regulator?
